The diagram above shows a cubic gas tank. One-fifth of the volume of the tank is filled with gas. If the fuel costs $$0.0016$ per cubic centimeter, how much would it cost to fill the tank to capacity?
question.worked_solution:
The length of $7\,\text{cm}$ shown in the diagram represents one-fifth of the tank's side length. Therefore, the length of each side of the tank is

$$
5\cdot 7=35\,\text{cm}.
$$

The empty space in the cube is a rectangular prism that is $35\,\text{cm}$ long, $35\,\text{cm}$ wide, and $35-7=28\,\text{cm}$ high.

We can find the volume $V$ of the rectangular prism using the formula

$$
V=lwh,
$$

where $l$ is the length, $w$ is the width, and $h$ is the height of the solid.

Substituting 

$$
l=35\,\text{cm},\,w=35\,\text{cm},\,h=28\,\text{cm}
$$

into the formula, we obtain

$$
V=35\cdot 35\cdot 28=34\,300\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.
$$

Finally, to fill the tank to capacity, it would cost

$$
34\,300\cdot 0.0016=$54.88.
$$
